title: Online response minimizes mixed payoff
statement: Let $G$ be a finite zero-sum game with $M\ge1$ row actions and $N\ge1$ column actions, and with every payoff in $[0,1]$. For any learning rate $\eta\in\bbr$, horizon $T$, round $t<T$, and column action $j$, let $j_s$ be the online column response at round $s$, and let the Hedge distribution at round $t$ be formed from the losses $1-G(i,j_s)$ for $s<T$. Then the payoff against the response $j_t$ under this distribution is at most the payoff against $j$; that is, $\sum_i p_t(i)G(i,j_t)\le\sum_i p_t(i)G(i,j)$.
hypotheses_covered: $G$ is a zero-sum game with payoffs in $[0,1]$
replaced:
Let $G$ be a finite zero-sum game with $M \ge 1$ row actions and $N \ge 1$ column
actions, let $\eta \in \mathbb{R}$ be a learning rate, and let $T$ be a horizon.
Write $j_s = \texttt{hedgeResponseNat}(G, \eta, s)$ for the online column
response at round $s$, and let $\ell = \texttt{ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq}(G, (j_s)_{s < T})$
be the loss sequence it induces for the row player.  Then for every round
$t < T$ and every fixed column $j$,
\[
  \sum_{i} \texttt{hedgeDist}(\eta, \ell, t)_i \, A(i, j_t)
  \;\le\;
  \sum_{i} \texttt{hedgeDist}(\eta, \ell, t)_i \, A(i, j),
\]
i.e.\ the played column $j_t$ gives the row player, mixing according to the
Hedge distribution at round $t$, no more payoff than any other column.
